newsitem.title: LEBANON: Monitors confirm rocket hit Israel from Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Monitors confirm rocket hit Israel from Lebanon.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon confirmed that at least one Katyusha rocket was fired from south Lebanon into Israel last Wednesday but did not reprimand Lebanon.

In a statement issued late on Friday, the group comprising the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel said the attack violated the U.S.-brokered April ceasefire understanding that bans firing at civilians in both Israel and Lebanon.
The attack caused no injuries. It was the second such strike since the ceasefire ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in which more than 200 people, mostly civilians, were killed.

"By unanimity, the Monitoring Group accepted as factual that at least one Katyusha rocket was fired into Israel from the area of El-Kleila in Lebanon," said the statement, issued after a seven-hour meeting called by Israel in the coastal town of Naqoura, headquarters of the U.N. peacekeepers in south Lebanon.
"It noted that this act ran counter to the April 26 understanding," the statement added.

Judicial sources said on Friday Lebanese authorities were interrogating two guerrillas of the radical Democractic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP) arrested on suspicion of firing the Katyusha rocket.
The monitoring group urged Beirut to intensify its efforts to prevent such incidents and "welcomed the latest measures taken by the Lebanese government in this respect".
Lebanon's Hizbollah and Amal movements, both of which are fighting the Israeli occupation of a border zone in south Lebanon, have denied any links to Wednesday's incident.
An earlier rocket attack on northern Israel on December 13 was verified by the monitors. They did not hold Lebanon directly responsible.
